title: Which of sync interval, compression, delay, momentum and robust aggregation sets the final loss of low-communication training?
lede: research programme (proposal stage): a predictive theory of DiLoCo-style low-communication training, testing on real small transformers the closed forms derived in about a dozen quadratic-model projects, with 16 references, hypotheses H1 to H6 and an ICML/NeurIPS workshop as the first target
summary: An open research programme rather than a finished project. DiLoCo-style training cuts communication by orders of magnitude, but choosing the sync interval, compressor and outer optimiser is still a sweep at every scale, and the best empirical scaling laws do not say why one axis costs more than another. This repository holds about a dozen closed-form results on a quadratic with gradient noise (a noise floor inflated by 1+ω under compression, a delay stability limit 2 sin(π/(4τ+2)), an optimal outer momentum that falls with the sync interval, a median that costs π/2 in variance). The programme asks whether those structural factors survive on trained transformers and compose, so that two or three measured constants per model size predict the final loss of configurations never run, as well as a refitted scaling law does. Six falsifiable hypotheses each state the result that would refute them. Milestone 1 is done: a simulated M-worker DiLoCo harness on a 0.41M-parameter GPT reproduces the synchronous loop exactly at M=1, H=1 and the quadratic closed form to 2% (ratio 0.983, 95% CI containing it). No result on the research question yet; the proposal's citations are not yet machine-checked because the registries were unreachable.
